title: Niagara Falls in 2 days: mist, tunnels, and a night under the lights
excerpt: A short two-day loop from the Canadian side — Table Rock, the tunnels behind the falls, Clifton Hill at night, and a quieter morning across the Niagara Parkway.
contentHtml:
I finally made it to Niagara with a simple plan: don’t rush the falls, and don’t pretend Clifton Hill is subtle. Two days on the Canadian side was enough to feel the spray, walk the tunnels, and still leave wanting one more sunrise.

This isn’t a checklist of every ticket — just what we actually did, and what I’d repeat.

days.label: Arrival & the roar
days.title: Arrive, Table Rock, and the first look

blocks.body: Dropped bags, walked straight to the rail at Horseshoe Falls. Stood longer than planned. Mist on the lens within five minutes.
Took the elevator down into the tunnels. The wall of water at the open portals is louder than any photo suggests. Poncho earned its keep.
Neon, fudge shops, and people-watching. Grabbed dinner nearby and walked back when the falls were lit. One slow loop along the rail before bed.
